_note: Medication and laboratory work-up for Elias Ward (Chapter 1), in ward-round case form using the ward-round catalogs. Approved by the owner on 2026-11-05 (docs/clinical_review_log.md). Aligned on 2026-11-05, at the owner's request ("have it agree in the most logical way"), with the owner-approved bedside encounter (data/elias_encounter.json): its history, vitals, lab results and order verdicts are the source of truth here. The lorazepam response is shown by the encounter; this work-up has no story effect of its own and shows no dose.

presentation.reason: Transferred for competency restoration. Stopped speaking four days before transfer; barely drinking, not eating, and lying in one position for hours.
presentation.history: Withdrawn for about a week, then mute. Haloperidol 5 mg intramuscular twice, six and five days before transfer, for agitation; no regular medication since and no benzodiazepine given. One admission at 24 with psychosis. Daily cannabis and weekend alcohol before arrest; in custody six weeks. No urine since yesterday afternoon.
presentation.mental_status: Mute, with no reliable nonverbal reply. Marked reduction in movement; posturing to be confirmed by structured bedside examination.
presentation.vitals: 07:30: T 37.6 °C, HR 108, BP 142/88, RR 18, SpO2 98% on air. On arrival: T 37.2 °C, HR 96.

ck.teaching: Needed with recent haloperidol, a rising temperature and pulse, and immobility: a raised CK supports neuroleptic malignant syndrome or muscle breakdown.

bmp.result: Sodium 147 mmol/L (slightly raised), urea raised, creatinine at the upper limit of normal, potassium and glucose normal: consistent with dehydration.
bmp.teaching: Dehydration and poor intake: check sodium and kidney function.

cbc.result: White cell count 11.2 (slightly raised); otherwise normal.
cbc.teaching: Infection and a raised white count belong in the differential of a rising temperature.

uds.teaching: Low yield after six weeks in custody, but reasonable in an unexplained change.

collateral.result: Call to his sister Claire requested; awaiting her reply.
collateral.teaching: She knows his baseline and the onset better than any packet.

neuro_exam.result: No lead-pipe rigidity or cogwheeling. No ankle clonus; reflexes normal. No grasp reflex.

physical_exam.result: Dry mucous membranes. Lay in one position overnight without turning.

start:lorazepam.feedback: First-line for suspected catatonia, and a good response supports the diagnosis. Re-examine afterwards with the same steps.

start:haloperidol.feedback: Antipsychotics can worsen catatonia and precipitate neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and he already has a rising pulse and temperature after recent haloperidol. Hold antipsychotics until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

start:risperidone.feedback: The same risk as any antipsychotic here: hold until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

start:olanzapine.feedback: The same risk as any antipsychotic here: hold until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

start:quetiapine.feedback: The same risk as any antipsychotic here: hold until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

start:aripiprazole.feedback: The same risk as any antipsychotic here: hold until catatonia and NMS are assessed.

start:lithium.feedback: Not while he is barely eating or drinking.

int:nutrition_hydration.feedback: Poor intake and no urine since yesterday afternoon: he needs fluid support and his fluid balance measured, with the medical team.

int:ect_referral.feedback: ECT is the treatment for catatonia that does not respond to lorazepam, or for malignant catatonia. Start with a lorazepam challenge and medical workup.

int:close_observation.feedback: He cannot eat, drink or ask for help on his own. Continue 1:1 observation with hourly vital signs and temperature.

cases.teaching: Catatonia after recent haloperidol, with a rising pulse and temperature: start a lorazepam challenge and re-examine, hold all antipsychotics, check CK, electrolytes and blood count for NMS and dehydration, and get the medical team to see him.
